solution: $\\sin^{4}x=\\bigl(\\tfrac12(1-\\cos2x)\bigr)^{2}=\\tfrac14(1-2\\cos2x+\\cos^{2}2x)=\\tfrac14\\bigl(1-2\\cos2x+\\tfrac12(1+\\cos4x)\bigr)=\\tfrac38-\\tfrac12\\cos2x+\\tfrac18\\cos4x$. Integrating from $0$ to $\\pi/2$: $\\int_{0}^{\\pi/2}\\tfrac38\,dx=\\tfrac{3\\pi}{16}$, while $\\int_{0}^{\\pi/2}\\cos2x\,dx=\\bigl[\\tfrac12\\sin2x\bigr]_{0}^{\\pi/2}=0$ and $\\int_{0}^{\\pi/2}\\cos4x\,dx=\\bigl[\\tfrac14\\sin4x\bigr]_{0}^{\\pi/2}=0$. Hence $I=\\frac{3\\pi}{16}$.
